Shows the MONO clock over Android\'s lock screen. Swipe up to reach your normal PIN, pattern or fingerprint unlock.
Allowed: the lock screen can appear after any app.
Not allowed: the lock screen only appears when MONO\'s home screen was open. Tap to allow.
Use this wallpaper on Android\'s lock screen
Couldn\'t set the lock screen wallpaper
Android does not let apps replace the secure lock screen or the always-on display. MONO\'s lock screen sits on top of it and never bypasses your PIN, password or biometrics.
On: a player card appears on the lock screen while music or video is playing or paused. MONO does not read your notifications.
Off: Android requires notification access for apps to see what is playing. Tap to allow MONO (it does not read your notifications).
Long-press empty space on the home screen to rearrange, remove or add apps. Recent apps only include apps opened from MONO.

Lets MONO turn the display off like the power button: double-tap the MONO lock screen, idle timeout and pocket protection. MONO does not read the screen, your input or any app content, and it receives no accessibility events.
Turn on "MONO screen off" in Accessibility to use double-tap to sleep
Turn screen off after %1$d s without touch
Screen-off access is off: double-tap and pocket sleep need "MONO screen off" in Accessibility. Without it, MONO hands over to Android\'s lock screen to sleep. Tap to open.
Battery optimisation: MONO is exempt (recommended for a Home app).
Battery optimisation is restricting MONO. Realme may freeze it during long standby, which can briefly show the stock launcher. Tap to allow.
Realme: App info → Battery usage → allow background activity

Copy and export use the selected apps, or every app shown when nothing is selected.
Asked Android to open it as a floating window
This device reports freeform (floating) window support. MONO\'s long-press menu offers \"Open as floating window\"; Android decides the final window mode.
This device does not report floating-window support to apps, so MONO cannot open apps as floating windows. MONO hides that option instead of pretending.
Why MONO can\'t copy Realme\'s gesture

Holding the Home gesture and dragging an app to a corner is handled by Android\'s system navigation together with Realme\'s own launcher. Android never sends navigation gestures to other launchers, and there is no public API to turn the current app into a floating window, so MONO cannot detect or reproduce this gesture without root or hidden APIs.

Realme UI\'s own Flexible/Floating windows are system features: try Smart Sidebar (swipe from the screen edge) → choose an app, or open Recents → the app card\'s menu → Floating window. Availability and names differ between Realme UI versions, and some builds hide these options while another launcher is the default.
Long-press an app on the home screen or in the drawer → Open as floating window.

A few Android settings let MONO do its job. Each one says why it\'s needed; only the default Home step is required. MONO never turns these on by itself — you choose in Android Settings, then come back here.
You can come back any time: MONO settings → Permission setup.
Makes MONO the screen you see when you press Home.
Lets the MONO lock screen appear after you used another app (Android 10+ rule). Without it, it only appears when MONO was open.
Lets MONO turn the screen off like the power button (double-tap, idle timeout, pocket). MONO reads nothing on screen.
Android requires it for apps to see what music or video is playing, for the lock-screen media card. MONO does not read your notifications.
Recommended for a Home app: stops Realme from freezing MONO in standby, which can briefly show the stock launcher.
Pick your city for weather (no location permission needed).

Since Android 13, apps installed from an APK file (not from an app store) can\'t receive Accessibility or Notification access until you allow it. This protects you from malicious downloads. Only you can allow it — no app can do it automatically.
Try to turn on %2$s for %1$s once. If you see \"Restricted setting\" (or the switch is greyed out), tap OK — this makes the next option appear.
Open %1$s\'s App info and tap ⋮ (top-right corner).
Tap \"Allow restricted settings\" and confirm with your PIN, pattern or fingerprint.
Go back to %1$s and turn on \"%2$s\". Then return here — this page updates by itself.
Restricted setting · For your security, this setting is currently unavailable.
Confirm with PIN, pattern or fingerprint
No ⋮ menu or no \"Allow restricted settings\": first try the switch once (step 1) and tap OK on the warning, then reopen App info.
Android 12 or older: there are no restricted settings — just turn the switch on.
Apps installed from Google Play or the Realme App Market are not restricted.
Realme UI paths: Settings → Apps → App management → the app → ⋮. Accessibility: Settings → Additional settings → Accessibility → Downloaded apps (or Installed services).
After reinstalling an APK, you may need to allow restricted settings again.
MONO only opens the right Settings pages and checks the result. It cannot change these settings itself.
